passages.text: We will ship the new platform in Q3 and we are raising full-year revenue guidance by 8%.
Demand is running well ahead of supply; every unit we build this year is already spoken for.
Gross margin will expand at least 200 basis points next quarter.
We expect to be free-cash-flow positive by the end of this fiscal year, full stop.
Our backlog covers two years of production at current run rates.
Pricing is holding and we do not see that changing this year.
We believe, depending on how the second half develops, we could see modest improvement.
If conditions allow, we should be in a position to revisit the buyback later in the year.
We expect, subject to supply availability, that volumes may recover somewhat.
It is possible that margins normalise, but there are a number of moving parts.
We are hopeful about the pipeline, though timing remains uncertain.
We think the trend is likely to continue, assuming no further macro deterioration.
Analyst: Will the new plant be profitable next year? Management: We are excited about the opportunity the plant represents for our customers.
Analyst: How many units did you sell in the region? Management: We do not break out results by geography.
Analyst: Why did the CFO leave? Management: We thank her for her contributions and are pleased with the transition.
Analyst: Is churn up or down quarter over quarter? Management: Our customers love the product, as the survey scores show.
Analyst: What is the timeline for regulatory approval? Management: We continue to work constructively with regulators.
Analyst: Did pricing pressure affect the quarter? Management: Let me step back and talk about our long-term strategy.
We missed our delivery target this quarter because the ramp took longer than we planned.
Frankly, our execution on the integration has not met our own expectations.
Churn rose in the small-business segment and we did not react quickly enough.
The inventory write-down reflects a forecasting error on our side.
We underestimated the cost of the recall; that is on us.
Yes, we lost that customer, and the loss will show up in next quarter's revenue.
Last quarter we said the facility would be closed by December; today we are describing it as a strategic long-term asset.
The 10-K lists the segment as loss-making, yet on this call it was presented as consistently profitable.
In February management guided to flat headcount; the prepared remarks now cite a 15% increase as always planned.
The CEO said pricing was raised across the board; the CFO said minutes later that list prices were unchanged.
Management called the product launch on schedule, while the filing from last week disclosed a two-quarter delay.
The buyback was described as completed, although the same call reported only half the authorisation used.

guidance.text: We are raising our full-year revenue outlook to a range of 4.2 to 4.4 billion, up from 4.0 to 4.2 billion.
Given the strength of the first half, we now expect operating margin at the high end of our prior range, and we are lifting the EPS outlook accordingly.
We are reiterating our full-year guidance provided in January; nothing in the quarter changes that view.
Our outlook for the year is unchanged: revenue growth of 8 to 10 percent and margins roughly flat.
Reflecting the slower ramp, we are reducing our full-year revenue guidance to 3.6 to 3.8 billion from 4.0 to 4.2 billion.
We now expect the year to come in below the range we gave in February, driven by the customer loss discussed earlier.
Thank you for joining. Today we will review the quarter's results and take your questions; we do not provide forward guidance.
The quarter's revenue was 1.1 billion and net income was 90 million. Turning to the balance sheet, cash stood at 300 million.
We are increasing our outlook for the year on the back of the new contract; we now see revenue of at least 2 billion versus 1.8 billion previously.
Because of the delay, the second-half outlook is lower than we planned: we are cutting the full-year forecast by roughly 10 percent.
